note: In some predatory and scavenger species (e.g., raptors, gulls, corvids), captured food is routinely carried elsewhere to consume, so carrying food on a single occasion is not a sure indication that they are carrying it to young. Behavior that supports this code includes carrying food in the same direction repeatedly and carrying food deliberately into nesting habitat, especially when passing suitable locations for consuming.

Some species construct multiple dummy nests or cavities that are not only used for nesting (e.g., woodpeckers and wrens). A follow-up visit is recommended to evaluate the persistence of breeding behavior.

P Pair should be used when both sexes of a sexually dimorphic species are observed interacting in correct habitat, or when prolonged interaction of non-sexually dimorphic species is observed.
